summary.headline: Bandhan Bank Q2 FY27 PAT rose 5.5x YoY to INR 622 crore, with ROA at 1.2% and ROE at 9.3%.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 showed a sharp earnings recovery: PAT of INR 622 crore (up 23.9% QoQ, 5.5x YoY) and operating profit of INR 1,556 crore (up 18.8% YoY). Net CD ratio fell to 89.5% from about 92% as deposits grew 4.7% QoQ without FCNR(B) support. Loan book grew 13.1% YoY to about INR 1.58 lakh crore, with the EEB book stabilising sequentially. CASA weakened as savings balances ran off after rate recalibration, and management flagged this as below expectations.

segments.name: EEB (Emerging Entrepreneur Business)
segments.commentary: Portfolio INR 52,616 crore, broadly flat QoQ and +1.7% YoY; de-growth arrested. Collection efficiency 99.3% vs 98.9% in Q1; EEB DPD pool fell to INR 1,529 crore from INR 1,842 crore; EEB slippages INR 655 crore.

segments.name: Wholesale Banking
segments.commentary: Grew 31.6% YoY and is now 34% of advances; management says wholesale ROA is improving and rising ROA supports overall ROA.

segments.name: Retail assets
segments.commentary: Grew 41.9% YoY, led by commercial vehicles, construction equipment, auto and gold loans; 11% of advances. Retail products remain not yet ROA-positive.

segments.name: Housing finance
segments.commentary: 22% of advances; growth impacted by verticalisation and asset-quality issues, with management saying impact may extend one more quarter.

segments.name: Microfinance (MFI)
segments.commentary: Book flat QoQ after several quarters of decline; management targets 8%-10% growth in Q3 and Q4. Current yield about 21.69%; new origination rates 23.5%-23.9%.

segments.name: Deposits
segments.commentary: Total INR 1.73 lakh crore, +9.2% YoY and +4.7% QoQ; retail deposits 72.7% of base; CASA INR 46,132 crore (+4.3% YoY), CASA ratio 26.7%; current accounts +36.9% YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 loan growth target of about 14% maintained; implies roughly 6% growth per half in H2 per analyst arithmetic.
Q4 FY27 exit ROA guidance of 1.2%-1.4% unchanged; 1.2% already achieved in Q2. Medium-term ROA aspiration 1.6%-1.8%, timing under review.
NIM expected to remain in 6.1%-6.2% range; repo-linked repricing from January 1 (Q4) could give a positive NIM impact.
Operating expense to total assets guidance of 4.2% unchanged.
Credit cost could improve from 1.8% to 1.7% per management's illustrative ROA bridge.
Full-year FY27 PSLC cost around INR 120 crore (about INR 31 crore per quarter); expected to be near zero in FY28.
Employee cost assumed to stay at about similar levels through Q4 FY27 (analyst reference INR 1,300-1,400 crore run rate).
Deposit growth to remain slightly above loan growth; management acknowledged deposit growth needs to be faster.
ECL transition impact estimated at about INR 2,200 crore against capital, with RBI five-year amortisation window; flow impact of 15-20 bps per quarter.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 2,001 branches (13 added in quarter) and 4,414 banking units (14 added).
Housing finance centres converted into branches under branch banking; onboarding, underwriting and operations segregated.
Credit card launched in the quarter with four variants: Sparks, Ignite, Flare and Lumina.
Technology platform replacement generated about INR 50 crore annual savings (INR 12 crore per quarter), benefit received in Q2; ongoing technology spend continues.
demand_pricing: Processing fee income +30% YoY, driven by higher EEB disbursements and a 25 bps processing-charge increase in February.
Third-party distribution income +26% YoY and +26% QoQ; ARC-related income +16% YoY; treasury gains on investment sales +39% QoQ.
Bancassurance: draft commission cap could cut third-party income; management has not completed a detailed study and says mitigation levers include product mix, mutual funds and wholesale fee income.
Savings account balances fell after rate recalibration; Annapurna scheme flows (about INR 4,000 crore monthly, West Bengal) shifted timing and affected CASA.
Retail sub-scale products (book INR 2,000-3,000 crore each) are not yet ROA-positive; management expects positive ROA in two to three quarters.
Industry deposit comparisons are harder as peers used FCNR(B) leverage facilities that Bandhan did not have.

qa_highlights.question: How much SA attrition and cost of funds/NIM pressure is expected in H2 after the SA rate cut?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said deposit costs have not come under pressure, cost of funds should moderate, and it still expects NIM in the 6.1%-6.2% range. CASA dip was attributed partly to Annapurna timing; new digital features and credit cards are expected to help.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ECL day-one impact and credit cost implications?
qa_highlights.answer: Transition impact estimated at about INR 2,200 crore based on March 2026 flow rates, hitting capital not P&L, with a five-year amortisation window. Flow impact 15-20 bps per quarter; management expects a favourable change as DPD pools improve.

qa_highlights.question: Could bancassurance income fall about 60% under the draft norms?
qa_highlights.answer: Management has not completed a detailed study; says insurance business is predominantly retail and semi-urban, consent-based, with no credit-linked insurance, and expects to offset a large part through other fee lines.

qa_highlights.question: Is processing fee growth sustainable, and what is the implied H2 loan growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Processing fee growth is tied to disbursements and expected to continue. Management maintains 14% full-year loan growth target and aims for deposit growth slightly above loan growth.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Assam SMA uptick and is EEB slippage likely to ease?
qa_highlights.answer: Four districts moved to moratorium (INR 406 crore), with 5% additional provision and over 96% of the book standard. Assam SMA-0 rose from 0.8% to 1.3% due to floods; management sees no material impact from Karnataka, Maharashtra or Andhra Pradesh climate-affected areas.

qa_highlights.question: How will repo changes affect NIM and what share of the book is repo-linked?
qa_highlights.answer: Repo changes apply to existing loans from the next quarter start, so the January change lands in Q4; Q3 largely unaffected. About 49% repo-linked, 3% MCLR, 48% fixed. Management does not expect a major effect this year; 25 bps repo move transmits about 10-11 bps.

qa_highlights.question: Why did wholesale and retail grow faster and how is opex trending?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets one-third each of EEB, wholesale and retail/housing; EEB share now about 33%. Employee cost is up about 20% due to the new Labour Code wage norms; headcount broadly stable for three quarters.

risks_watch: SA balances and CASA ratio (26.7%) under pressure after rate recalibration; watch whether attrition continues into Q3.
Bancassurance commission cap: management has not quantified impact; analyst cited a possible about 60% fee hit if draft norms are adopted as proposed.
Housing business: management says disruption may extend one more quarter into Q3.
EEB stress from Assam floods (SMA-0 at 1.3%) and drought areas; Maharashtra is 2.6% of EEB book.
Deposit growth lag (9.2% YoY) versus industry boosted by FCNR(B) flows; bulk deposits used for liquidity management.
ECL transition impact of about INR 2,200 crore to be recalculated on March 2027 portfolio.
summary.management_tone: Confident on earnings momentum and asset-quality trends, but cautious and somewhat defensive on savings deposits, housing and deposit growth. Several answers were hedged ("hopeful", "we are working on it") when asked about bancassurance impact and H2 growth, with no quantified bancassurance estimate given.
key_quotes: Our performance during the quarter demonstrates the underlying resilience of the franchise.
We do not intend to use bulk funding as a structural source to drive loan growth.
There is no change in our guidance.
We should have performed much better in home loans.

adds.what: 13 branches added in quarter (2,001 total) and 14 banking units added (4,414 total)

growth.why: Management reiterated around 14% FY27 advances growth, with Q2 loan book up 13.1% YoY and wholesale and retail growing 31.6% and 41.9%, but gave no specific capacity or order numbers behind the H2 pace, which implies only about 6% per half.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM guided flat at 6.1%-6.2% (Q2 at 6.1% vs 6.2% in Q1), with repo-linked repricing from January 1 expected to help Q4; 49% of book is repo-linked but 25 bps repo move transmits only about 10-11 bps, so impact is limited.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Branch network grew by 13 to 2,001 and banking units by 14 to 4,414 in Q2, and housing finance centres are being converted into branches; the pace is steady but modest, not a major capacity step-up.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 loan growth target of about 14% is held, but Q2 was 13.1% YoY, so H2 needs roughly 6% per half; MFI is guided at 8%-10% growth in Q3 and Q4 and deposits are growing 9.2% YoY, slightly below the loan book.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is not discussed and no new plant or major capex is flagged; the spend focus is on technology, with about INR 50 crore annual savings from the platform replacement already received.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q4 exit ROA guidance of 1.2%-1.4% is unchanged even though Q2 already hit 1.2%, and FY27 loan growth of about 14%, opex-to-assets of 4.2% and credit cost guidance were all held rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Bancassurance draft commission cap could cut third-party income, with an analyst-cited possible fee hit of about 60% not quantified by management; housing disruption may run one more quarter; SA/CASA attrition (CASA ratio 26.7%) and Assam SMA-0 rising to 1.3% add risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Credit card launched in Q2 with four variants (Sparks, Ignite, Flare, Lumina); retail sub-scale products of INR 2,000-3,000 crore each are expected to turn ROA-positive in two to three quarters.

rows.label: Bancassurance commission cap under draft norms
rows.why: Analyst cited a possible about 60% hit to bancassurance fee income if draft norms pass as proposed; management has not completed a study, and mitigation via product mix, mutual funds and wholesale fees is only hinted.

rows.label: ECL transition impact on capital
rows.why: About INR 2,200 crore capital impact at March 2026 flow rates, amortised over five years under RBI norms, with flow impact of 15-20 bps per quarter; to be recalculated on March 2027 portfolio.

rows.label: Technology platform savings
rows.why: Platform replacement is generating about INR 50 crore annual savings (INR 12 crore per quarter), already received in Q2, though employee cost is up about 20% from Labour Code wage norms.
